newsitem.title: INDIA: Political crisis won't hit investors-India's Singh.
newsitem.headline: Political crisis won't hit investors-India's Singh.

text.p: Former finance minister and Congress leader Manmohan Singh said on Sunday that a change in government should not deter foreign investors.

"Why should it affect investor confidence. The economy has now acquired a momentum of its own," Singh told Reuters soon after his party decided to withdraw support for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 15-group United Front coalition government.
Singh said there was a broad political consensus in the country on basic economic policies.
He said the world should by now recognise that political changes in India were a reality.
"The underlying cross currents are such that the fundamentals of the economy will determine what will happen," he said.
Congress President Sitaram Kesri said on Sunday the party was formally staking its bid to form a new federal government.
The Congress party said it might amend some of the budget proposals of Deve Gowda's government if the party succeeded in its declared bid to head a new coalition.
Congress general secretary Ghulam Nabi Azad told Reuters: "We will see what changes are needed and implement them."
A Commerce Ministry spokeswoman told Reuters India would announce its new export-import policy as scheduled on Monday, and the announcement would not be affected by political changes.
The current policy expires on Monday and a new policy has to take effect on April 1.

Singh, architect of India's radical economic reforms programme launched in 1991, said a change in the government would not cause any crisis in the federal budget for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) presented in parliament on February 28.
"The vote on account has been passed already," he said. A vote on account is taken for four months, Singh said.
"Long before that all these things should be settled."
A vote on account is a temporary measure that authorises the government to borrow money from the treasury to meet its expenses. The budget has not yet been approved by parliament.
Singh declined to say if he anticipated regaining the finance minister's job.
"How do I know. We will cross that bridge when we reach there," he said.
